newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus leader in Moscow for union talks, signing.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader in Moscow for union talks, signing.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko arrived in Moscow on Thursday for meetings with Russian President Boris Yeltsin to iron out differences over a controversial union deal one day before its planned signing.
"I came to seal things 'de jure' the things which have already happened 'de facto'," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Lukashenko as saying as he arrived.
Lukashenko had already reiterated that Belarus would remain a soverign state, rejecting talk that a closer alliance in the form of a federation could be formed.
"We have a certain limit -- our Soviet experience. Under the Soviet Union we (Belarus) had our own United Nations membership," Lukashenko said before he left Minsk.
Yeltsin said earlier this week that he saw Russia and Belarus merging into a single federative state by the end of the integration process, comments which prompted an angry reaction in Minsk.
Belarus negotiators are seeking a tight union between two independent states each of which would have equal rights.
Yeltsin and the hardline Belarus president, who signed a short and largely declarative union treaty last month, are expected to fill it out with a more detailed charter on Friday.
The leaders still appear at odds on the most important issues, including the powers of the future union and its ultimate aim, but both have said they planned to settle differences on Thursday.
Lukashenko also said in Minsk that he hoped other former Soviet states would join the union soon. "I am convinced that we will not be alone with Russia," he said.
